title: Functions of Ingredients: Stretch
welcome_lead: Stretch into raising agents, stabilisers and clever ingredient swaps.
meta_desc: Stretch GCSE ingredients: raising agents, stabilisers, dietary substitutes.
final_note: Substitution is creativity backed by science.

Chemical raising agent of bicarb and acid.

walkthroughs.body_html: Biological raising uses yeast, fermenting sugars into CO2 — bread. Chemical raising uses baking powder or bicarbonate of soda reacting with acid to release CO2 — cakes, scones. Mechanical raising whisks in air — sponges, meringues.

Stabilisers like xanthan gum and lecithin keep oil and water mixed and stop ice crystals forming in ice cream. They are common in commercial food but you can find natural equivalents — egg yolk, mustard — in home cooking.

For dietary needs, swap with thought. A 'flax egg' (1 tbsp ground flax + 3 tbsp water) replaces an egg's binding role in vegan baking. Aquafaba (chickpea brine) whisks like egg white. Gluten-free flour blends usually need xanthan to mimic gluten's stretch.
